findings.cross_file_justification: evals/harness/execute-agent.sh (resolve_toggles) consumes LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES from the inherited environment; evals/harness/run-arms.sh (run_trial) and evals/harness/run-eval.sh (both diff-touched) invoke it without clearing that variable, and run-eval.sh now stamps rows with env.LOA_EVAL_ARM // "baseline".
findings.description: resolve_toggles() prefers LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES over the suite's ab.arms[] declaration and does not require arm mode (LOA_EVAL_ARM set) or a non-baseline arm. With LOA_EVAL_ARM unset, ARM_MODE=false and ARM=baseline, yet apply_toggles still runs: companion_voice even creates an empty sandbox .loa.config.yaml (`: > "$cfg"`) because the prompt-tree config is only copied in arm mode. run-arms.sh validates arm ids against the suite but passes the parent environment through, so a stale exported LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES makes every arm in a batch run the same toggles while rows are labelled per `arm`. The same leak into run-eval.sh makes a production gate run execute toggled prompt material while recorded as arm=baseline. The header guarantee ('an arm never silently runs as its baseline') has no converse; arm_toggles is recorded but compare.sh/arms-report key on `arm`. This also lets an environment variable weaken `flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice`, a floor_keys entry in .claude/data/floor.yaml, inside gate runs.
findings.failure_mode: Control-arm and production recall results are mislabelled: all arms (or the baseline gate) run with identical, undeclared toggles; the A/B verdict and the regression gate compare the wrong things and the floor key is silently weakened in the sandbox the gate measures.
findings.suggested_fix: In execute-agent.sh: honor LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES only when ARM_MODE=true and ARM != baseline, and exit 2 if ARM == baseline resolves to a non-empty toggle set. In run-arms.sh run_trial: pass `LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES=` (or `env -u LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES`) so the suite declaration is authoritative. In run-eval.sh: refuse (or at least warn and record) when LOA_EVAL_ARM/LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES are set for a non-arm run. Have compare-ab.py/arms-report.py assert executor.arm_toggles equals the suite's declared toggles for that arm.

findings.description: run-arms.sh's verify_corpus only iterates the entries listed in SHA256SUMS and checks that each listed file exists and matches. It never walks the fixture directory, so a file added under pr-NN/head/, pr-NN/base/ or alongside PR.md that is not in SHA256SUMS passes both the batch-start check and the per-trial check, is copied into the sandbox by sandbox.sh, and the row is still stamped `fixture_verified: true` with an unchanged corpus_sha256_at_trial. seed-corpus-from-record.sh's check() does detect '(not listed)' files, so the two verifiers disagree and run-arms.sh uses the weaker one.
findings.failure_mode: Mid-run or pre-run additions to a fixture (extra source files, instruction-bearing markdown, a planted CLAUDE.md) reach the agent under test undetected while the batch MANIFEST and every row claim the frozen corpus was verified; the drift-stop (exit 3) never fires.
findings.suggested_fix: In verify_corpus, os.walk the corpus (or the one fixture's pr-NN/, labels/pr-NN.*, manifests/pr-NN.json) and fail on any regular file not present in SHA256SUMS, mirroring check() in seed-corpus-from-record.sh; alternatively call `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check` at batch start and keep the per-fixture walk per trial.

findings.anchor: # Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
findings.cross_file_justification: evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh (new) copies changed files of the Loa repo's own sprints into pr-NN/head and pr-NN/base; evals/harness/execute-agent.sh (new toggle code) promises every arm sees exactly the toggled sandbox .claude/ and config. Both are in the diff.
findings.description: The seed's exclusion list (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) does not exclude CLAUDE.md or .claude/** from fixture content. The record fixtures (pr-11..pr-18) are cut from this repository, whose root CLAUDE.md is `@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`. Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files found in subdirectories on demand when the agent reads files beneath them, and resolves `@` imports relative to that file. When a sprint's base..head touched CLAUDE.md and/or .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md, the sandbox contains head/CLAUDE.md -> head/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md (with the Karpathy section intact) and the agent under test picks it up while reviewing head/. That bypasses the karpathy_block / rule_files toggles and the 'every arm sees the same config' invariant, and gives fixture content instruction authority over the agent being measured. I could not see sandbox.sh's layout, so this is conditional on head/ and base/ being materialised as plain directories inside the workspace.
findings.failure_mode: An arm declared as karpathy_block=false (or rule_files=false) runs with the removed instructions re-injected from the fixture itself; the toggle 'verified absent' check only looks at the materialised .claude/ tree, so the arm passes verification yet measures the wrong condition. More generally, fixture markdown becomes a prompt-injection channel into the executor.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude CLAUDE.md, .claude/** and any *.md whose path is loaded as agent instructions from fixture base/ and head/ in seed-corpus-from-record.sh (and build-review-corpus.sh), or rename them (e.g. CLAUDE.md -> CLAUDE.md.txt) in the fixture copy with the rename recorded in fixture.yaml. Additionally have execute-agent.sh refuse (exit 2) when any CLAUDE.md or .claude/ directory exists under the workspace outside the materialised prompt tree, and add an arm-toggles.bats case that plants head/CLAUDE.md and asserts the executor's effective instruction set via STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR.

findings.description: The --batch allow-list regex accepts the literal names `.` and `..`. With `--batch ..`, BATCH_DIR resolves to $RESULTS_ROOT, so MANIFEST.json, STATUS.json, run.log, <arm>/results.jsonl, the .lock and .jobs directories are written beside the suite directories and cleanup() runs `rm -rf` on $RESULTS_ROOT/.jobs and .lock. With `--batch .`, the per-batch STATUS.json overwrites the suite-level aggregate that report.sh --arms and the Sprint 2 gate read. The operator controls --results-dir anyway, so this is a hardening gap rather than an escalation, but the regex is clearly meant to confine the batch to one child directory.
findings.failure_mode: Suite-level STATUS.json / MANIFEST.json are clobbered or scattered into the results root; later report/gate runs read a batch's state as the suite aggregate.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject `.` and `..` explicitly (e.g. `[[ "$BATCH" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ && "$BATCH" != '.' && "$BATCH" != '..' ]]`), or require the first character to be alphanumeric. Apply the same rule to --suite/--results-dir derived paths used in rm -rf.

findings.description: Transport-failure classification greps the agent's own output (agent-output.json result text) and stderr with very broad patterns (`network`, `socket hang up`, `5[0-9][0-9] `). When execute-agent.sh exits 1 for an agent-side reason (max turns, is_error, refusal), a review that merely mentions networking or a 5xx status code is reclassified as transport failure and the trial is re-run once after --retry-wait. The agent under test thereby influences whether it gets a second attempt, and the classification differs by fixture content.
findings.failure_mode: Biased recall figures (retried agent errors are counted as if the first attempt never happened) and doubled cost/time on fixtures whose subject matter happens to contain the keywords; the arm with more verbose output benefits more.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify on structured CLI fields only: executor.json exit_code 124/137/143, agent-output.json `.subtype == "missing"` / `.api_error_status`, and the system `model_refusal_fallback`/error events in events.jsonl. If free-text matching on stderr is kept, drop `network` and the bare `5xx ` pattern and never grep the result text.

findings.cross_file_justification: run-arms.sh reuses a cached worktree under $HOME/.cache/loa/cycle-129 as EVAL_PROMPT_TREE; execute-agent.sh (diff-touched) records the prompt-tree identity from the commit object (HEAD:.claude), not from the working tree it actually copies.
findings.description: The 'pinned source must be pristine' check uses `git status --porcelain`, which omits ignored files. A previously used worktree can carry ignored artefacts (for the Loa repo typically .loa.config.yaml, .claude/settings.local.json, .run/, caches) that execute-agent.sh copies into every arm's sandbox in arm mode (`cp "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml"`), yet prompt_tree_sha is computed from the commit tree so the recorded identity never changes. MANIFEST.json records source_worktree but no digest of the materialised tree.
findings.failure_mode: All arms of a batch inherit an unpinned, unrecorded config or local settings from the cache directory; the batch is reported as reproducible at source_commit while it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `git -C "$WORKTREE" status --porcelain --ignored` (or `git clean -ndx`) to be empty, or always `git worktree remove --force` and re-add per batch. In execute-agent.sh, record a sha256 of the materialised $WORKSPACE/.claude, CLAUDE.md and .loa.config.yaml in executor.json so compare/arms-report can assert all arms saw identical bytes modulo the declared toggles.

findings.description: The seed copies verbatim repository history into a tracked eval corpus (and run-arms.sh later commits review.md/audit.md artifacts). Redaction and title-dropping rely on nine regexes that miss common secret shapes: PEM private keys (-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----), JWTs, GitHub fine-grained/app tokens (github_pat_, ghs_, ghu_), Google API keys (AIza...), Stripe/Twilio keys, generic `api_key=`/`token:` assignments, and .env-style KEY=value. The two generic patterns use `[^"']{8,}` and `\s*`, which match newlines, so a `password = "` followed by lines without quotes is collapsed into one REDACTED-TEST-SECRET token across several lines, contradicting the 'line numbers never move' invariant and silently misaligning every anchor below it in head/ and head.diff. The header says no-secrets.sh gates every written file, which I could not inspect; if its coverage equals these regexes the gaps are real.
findings.failure_mode: Real credentials from a sprint's history land in a committed fixture corpus and in committed run artifacts; or a benign multi-line match shifts anchors so planted-defect recall is graded against the wrong lines without any error.
findings.suggested_fix:
Make redaction line-local (`[^"'
]{8,}`, `[ 	]*`) and assert `redacted.count("
") == original.count("
")`, failing the seed otherwise. Extend SECRET_RX with PEM, JWT, github_pat_/ghs_/ghu_, AIza, and generic high-entropy assignment patterns, or delegate detection to a dedicated scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog) run on the fixture directory before freeze; keep no-secrets.sh as the final gate and make the seed fail (not redact) when a match lands in a file whose anchors matter.

findings.description: The karpathy_block toggle promises Karpathy rows are removed from the sandbox .claude/data/constraints.json when present, but the removal is a `jq ... && mv` list: under `set -e` a jq failure (unexpected JSON shape, non-array `constraints`) does not abort the function, the original file is left untouched, a stray .tmp remains, and no post-condition check runs. arm_evidence then records only the CLAUDE.loa.md line count, so the arm passes the 'verified absent' gate while constraints.json still carries the rows. This contradicts the header's 'a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2' rule for this toggle only.
findings.failure_mode: A karpathy_block=false arm runs with Karpathy constraints still delivered through constraints.json (hooks or skills that read it), so the measured effect is attenuated without any trace in executor.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the jq step with explicit error handling (`|| { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block: constraints.json rewrite failed" >&2; return 2; }`), then verify `jq -e '[.constraints[]? | tostring | test("karpathy";"i")] | any | not' "$cj"` and record the removed-row count in arm_evidence.

findings.cross_file_justification: execute-agent.sh records whatever LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT says as source_commit; compare.sh (diff-touched usage text) now treats source_commit skew as the validity criterion for control-arm comparisons.
findings.description: source_commit is taken verbatim from the environment with no format check and no cross-check against the prompt tree actually materialised ($prompt_tree_commit). run-arms.sh passes a verified SHA, but any other caller (run-eval.sh, ad-hoc runs, tests) can set LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT to an arbitrary string, so two trials from different prompt trees can present identical source_commit values and pass compare.sh's skew check, while run-eval.sh's new row fields prefer this value over prompt_tree_commit.
findings.failure_mode: The provenance field that compare.sh and arms-report use to decide whether arms are comparable can be made to agree when the underlying prompt trees differ, producing a 'valid' comparison of unlike things.
findings.suggested_fix: In execute-agent.sh validate `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` and exit 2 when LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT is set but is not a prefix of (or equal to) `git -C "$PROMPT_TREE" rev-parse HEAD`; always record prompt_tree_commit alongside and have compare-ab.py/arms-report.py assert they agree.
